transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Evelyn Cho (Nimbus HoS), Marco Benitez (Nimbus Platform Eng), Sara O'Neill (Nimbus ML)

Summary:
Quick discovery for embeddings/rerank pilot. Nimbus is deciding between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a high-throughput hybrid retrieval stack. Main concerns: embedding dimensionality, quantization impact on recall, vector DB fanout and tail latency, and security/compliance (KMS / audit logs).

Topics Covered:
- Current infra and QPS/latency SLOs
- Embedding dimension tradeoffs (128/256/768/1024) and index size/cost
- Quantization (8-bit vs 4-bit) and measured recall drop for rerank
- Hosting options: Hosted API, Dedicated GPU pool, Private VPC/on-prem
- Hybrid routing and fallback to local index vs remote vector DB
- Benchmarks, pilot scope, and next steps

Action items summarized above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - we'll give a quick intro. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood side, and Priya is our SE.
[00:14] Priya: Hi. Quick asks from us: can you share qps, percentiles, current embedding dims, and whether you're using an external vector DB now?
[00:25] Evelyn: Yeah, thanks. I'm Evelyn - Head of Search at Nimbus. We're currently ~2.5k qps peak for serving search, tail latency SLO 150ms 95th. We're using Qdr... Qd-rant? qdrant in prod for the index, CPU nodes, and some faas for ranking rerank.
[00:42] Marco: Sorry, I wanted to add we also have peaks up to 4.5k for promos. Most queries ask topk 50 then rerank top10. We do a hybrid flow: candidate fanout from vector DB -> transformer reranker.
[01:02] Jordan: Great. So main decision: keep hosted for ease vs Dedicated for predictable throughput vs Private for data residency/compliance. Can you describe sensitivity to embedding dims?
[01:16] Sara: We're testing 768 dims currently for semantic search. We think 256 might be sufficient for some use-cases but worried about recall drop for financial queries. Also storage costs are non-trivial.
[01:30] Priya: Right, dimension reduction reduces disk and memory for the vector DB, and also affects ANN latency. But quantization can be complementary — 8-bit can give big storage wins with small recall hit. Have you tried PQ or OPQ?
[01:48] Evelyn: We did product quantization (PQ) in a prior experiment with big recall hits in edge cases. That was on CPU and older libs. We're curious about Redwood's quantization/FP8 pipeline since Priya mentioned quantization-friendly runtime.
[02:07] Priya: Yeah, our runtime supports quantized kernels and we do end-to-end evals with your data to get delta-recall for reranking. In many cases 8-bit LLM embeddings plus a learned reranker keeps downstream metrics nearly identical. But it depends on model head and training.
[02:28] Jordan: A practical question — if you go Hosted, we can do a quick pilot with a hosted model variant and prefix caching. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and lower tail variance; Private gives you VPC, KMS, audit logs. Any must-have for Nimbus on compliance?
[02:45] Evelyn: SOC 2 is a must, and we need KMS integration and audit logs. Private would be ideal for some regulated flows, but initial pilot can be on Hosted as long as logs are auditable.
[02:59] Marco: And network egress — we want a design where vector DB can live in our VPC and Redwood calls are inside peered network. Is that possible?
[03:12] Priya: Yes, for Private we do VPC peering and a customer-managed control plane. For Dedicated we can colocate in your region with private connectivity options. For Hosted we'd recommend a hybrid: keep vector DB in your network, export embeddings via secure pipeline, or use proxied calls. We'll share architecture diagrams.
[03:32] Jordan: Quick note about routing: many customers do hybrid top-k routing — do a cheap ANN top-200 from the vdb, then cut to top-20 for the reranker. That reduces expensive rerank tokens. Are you doing that now?
[03:48] Marco: Yes that's our flow, but we see tail latency spikes when the DB fanout crosses shards. We're exploring sharded indexes with smarter replica routing to avoid cross-shard hits.
[04:05] Priya: On the runtime side we have smart routing and fallback to local model variants. Also we support per-request policies: prefer-low-latency or prefer-low-cost which can route to smaller quantized variants. The fallbacks will keep the app online if the vector DB is slow.
[04:24] Evelyn: Can you explain the cost tradeoffs? I want numbers for storing 100M vectors at 768 dims vs 256 dims and quantized to 8-bit.
[04:36] Jordan: We'll put detailed numbers in the pricing sheet, but rough math: 100M * 768 * 4 bytes ~= 307GB * no that math is off — hmm sorry, brain slip — let me recalc in the sheet. But rough idea: 768 dims full-float is about 3x the size of 256 dims; 8-bit brings it close to 1/4 the full-float size. Storage + egress + query cost combine. We'll include an estimate.
[05:03] Sara: That's helpful. Also regarding recall: have you seen specific guidance on when to drop dims vs quantize? For example: 512->256 often OK for generic embeddings but financial text needs more nuance.
[05:16] Priya: Exactly. We usually recommend running an eval set; we can run automatic regression tests vs your golden queries to measure MRR/Recall@k. If the reranker is strong, you can compress more on the candidate side.
[05:31] Jordan: We should talk about performance testing. Priya, can you sketch the microbenchmark plan?
[05:36] Priya: Plan: take a 100k sample of Nimbus's index, run 3 dims (256/512/768) with raw float32 vs 8-bit quant. Measure QPS and 95/99 p95/p99 latency for top200 and top50 fanouts. Also run end-to-end rerank cost per query and delta-recall using your evaluation set. We'll include GPU latency from the inference engine and vector DB query latency.
[06:03] Marco: On the vector DB side, we use HNSW in Qdrant but the sharding is custom. If we move to Hosted index or use your recommended flow, is there an option to keep an external DB and use Redwood just for embeddings + rerank?
[06:18] Priya: Yes. Many customers keep their vector DB (Qdrant / Pinecone) and call Redwood for embedding generation + reranking. We also support inserting embeddings generated by Redwood into your DB automatically as a controlled pipeline.
[06:34] Evelyn: How do you handle consistency if we re-embed millions of documents for a new model or new dim? We can't have prolonged reindexing windows.
[06:45] Priya: We support progressive reindexing and snapshot-based rollouts. You can pin model versions and do canary re-embed a subset to measure deltas. Our Optimize tooling suggests re-embed batch sizes and background reindex throttles.
[06:59] Jordan: Security question: where are embeddings stored for Hosted pilots? Are they encrypted at rest? Who can access them?
[07:08] Priya: Hosted stores embeddings in encrypted buckets, access controlled by IAM, and we integrate with customer KMS for enterprise customers. For Private, you control keys and storage. We'll attach SOC2 and audit docs.
[07:24] Marco: On throughput — we need predictable tail latency at 95/99. Are there autoscaling knobs for Dedicated to handle spikes?
[07:34] Priya: Yes Dedicated has reserved GPU pools and configurable autoscaling and burst policies to hit latency SLOs. We can configure cold-start warm pools to reduce tail latency.
[07:47] Speaker 1: (mumble) do you support 4-bit quant?
[07:50] Priya: We have experimental 4-bit support but with more variance in recall. For production we recommend 8-bit for embeddings. 4-bit can be good for cruft models but needs evaluation.
[08:02] Evelyn: If we go Dedicated, what's the expected per-token or per-embedding cost relative to Hosted?
[08:09] Jordan: Dedicated is typically lower per-unit once you commit capacity, but you pay reserved monthly. Hosted is pay-as-you-go and faster to start. We'll send a concrete example in the pricing sheet.
[08:21] Sara: About reranker token counts — we're currently using a 2k token reranker for context which is expensive. Any suggestions?
[08:28] Priya: You can reduce reranker tokens by doing candidate pruning and using a smaller distilled reranker. Also caching repeated queries helps a lot. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching settings and sequence-length truncation heuristics.
[08:43] Jordan: Let's demo a small perf story: typical flow — user query -> vector DB top200 -> rerank top10 on Redwood -> return. We can optionally run a cheap lexical filter before candidate generation.
[08:57] Marco: The problem is cross-shard fanout. If top200 touches 5 shards, latency multiplies. Any guidance?
[09:06] Priya: We recommend shard-aware routing: route to a single replica responsible for the partition when possible, or prefer locality-based reads. We can also maintain warmed-hot partitions in Dedicated pools to reduce cross-shard overhead.
[09:22] Evelyn: Can Redwood's runtime host an ANN index for us? Like store a compact index inside your Dedicated pool?
[09:30] Priya: We have options: 1) keep index on your VDB, 2) Redwood-managed index with private tenancy, or 3) hybrid where we keep a fast hot index (top slices) inside the runtime and cold store in your DB. The hybrid model often reduces tail lat significantly.
[09:49] Jordan: Towards next steps — we propose a 2-week pilot: Redwood runs 100k sample in Hosted with 256/768 dims + 8-bit, run recall/regression, and measure end-to-end latency. If Nimbus likes results, move to Dedicated pilot with capacity commit. Thoughts?
[10:06] Evelyn: Sounds good. Need to check legal for data sync. We'll want the security docs before pilot start.
[10:12] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll attach SOC2, architecture diagrams, and proposed pilot scope.
[10:20] Sara: Quick question — for evaluation, do you prefer offline labeled queries or live canary traffic?
[10:26] Priya: Start offline with your golden queries to measure recall, then do a small live canary to validate latency and real traffic characteristics. We'll help tune the thresholds.
[10:36] Marco: About the reranker cost — can Redwood run the reranker inside our VPC or does it need to cross the network?
[10:44] Priya: In Private deployments, the runtime runs inside your VPC and the calls are local. For Hosted, we proxy or route via secure peering if available. Dedicated can be colocated in your region with private connectivity.
[10:58] Jordan: There's a note about KV cache — we have a prefix/KV cache that stores recent context to avoid recompute. That can shrink costs for repeated queries.
[11:10] Evelyn: Cool. Any pitfalls you've seen for finance customers specifically?
[11:15] Priya: Two big things: deusensitivity of embeddings (PII leakage) and regulatory requirements on audit logs and key control. Also for high-value queries, tiny recall drops can matter — run more conservative compression.
[11:29] Sara: We'll share a subset of queries and label some outputs to measure business metrics like CTR and fraud-detection accuracy.
[11:36] Jordan: Great. We'll also include a mini checklist for the pilot: sample dataset, qps profile, SLOs, security contacts, and pilot success criteria.
[11:47] Evelyn: Success criteria: no more than 2% drop in core recall on financial queries and p95 under 250ms end-to-end for rerank flow.
[11:58] Jordan: Noted. We'll include that in the pilot doc.
[12:06] Marco: One last question — for embedding ops, do you provide tooling to roll back to previous embeddings if regression happens?
[12:12] Priya: Yes we support model versioning and rollback. You can pin old embeddings and switch traffic via our rollout system if regressions appear.
[12:23] Jordan: Wrap-up: we'll send pricing, security docs, and pilot plan. Priya will run microbenchmarks and share numbers. Nimbus to send sample index and golden queries.
[12:33] Evelyn: Thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[12:36] Jordan: Thanks, bye.

Notes about transcript: occasional speaker IDs were fuzzy in the recording; some words transcribed incorrectly (e.g., Qdrant as "Qdr... Qd-rant?," KV cache transcribed as KV case).
